result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, including plain `mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟`. The two new tests pass, and `SourceFileFilterTest` still passes.

**Change:** In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, I replaced the two old rules (`.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`) with one rule, `(.*[/\\])?(__)?mock[^/\\]*[/\\].*`. The name after `mock` can be anything except a separator, so the match stays inside one folder name. Forward and backslash separators both work.

**Tests:** I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It checks the new folder names, the old ones (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`), and Windows paths. It also checks that `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are not test code.

I left the existing `mockapi/` and `[Mm]ocks/` rules untouched. The new rule is case-sensitive, so a folder named `MOCK/` is still not caught. Nothing is committed.
